scope: Read-only engine audit. This directory contains only deterministic development reproductions and evidence; no runtime changes, calibration or new 96 MP launch.

conclusion.established: The shipped native/JS bridge creates a borrowed Wasm view before Asyncify allocates its unwind stack. A successful automatic memory.grow can detach that view during broker readInto. The exact production error stack is reproducible with the unchanged shipped module and real broker on 8x8 pixels.
conclusion.limit: The 96MP journal contains no per-grow or failed store-id event. The mechanism is proved and precisely matches its stack, but its individual grow event was not recorded.
conclusion.writeRisk: A separate broker test proves silent truncation when write loops read source.length after an await and source detaches. No such truncation is established in the 96MP output.

nativeProof.deferredViewResult: Pass; same output hash as baseline. This is a fixture control, not a proposed blanket production async conversion.

causalSources.role: Borrow current HEAPU8 view and pass it into storage.
Writable broker awaits a response and then writes through the old view.
page_io_start invokes JS before asynchronous unwind.
page_io_wait enters Asyncify after I/O has begun.
Asyncify.allocateData allocates its stack through malloc.
Asyncify stack262144; next line enables growable memory.
Write loop can terminate early after source.length becomes zero.

counterEvidence: Heap is an unshared WebAssembly.Memory; other workers do not mutate or transfer this heap.
The failing read is on the writable broker branch, not the immutable L2 cache read branch.
The incoming Uint8Array is constructed immediately before set without another await; the destination is the retained borrowed view.
Read-only descriptor migration cannot directly detach a separate kernel linear memory; its barrier also waits for native task completion.
The minimal native reproduction has no descriptor migration, GPU or concurrent field; Asyncify alone suffices.
A simple fixed-memory safety margin is not a lifetime guarantee; allocator fragmentation and useful later allocations can consume it.

correctionArchitecture.invariant: No raw borrowed Wasm TypedArray may survive a possible unwind/await/grow. Retain a numeric pointer and fixed byte length, resolve a fresh view at the actual synchronous copy.
correctionArchitecture.suggestedContract: One common owned-memory-range adapter for read/write bridges. Async transports accept a renewable range or stage through a bounded accounted buffer, while synchronous resident/OPFS/cache-hit copies retain their fast path.
requirements: Save the original intended extent; never use detached view.length as the transaction progress bound.
Refresh after every asynchronous boundary and before every byte access, for source and destination.
Keep the native allocation alive and non-reentrant until I/O completion.
Propagate storage errors and cancellation; never reinterpret lifetime errors as OOM or silently retry the entire native field.
Test actual Asyncify-induced growth, read/write across multiple chunks, synchronous paths, temporary transports, cancellation, exact native outputs.
avoid: Making every resident byte page unconditionally asynchronous: this loses the existing sync fast path.
Increasing heap minima or keeping permanent spare RAM as the sole fix.
Catching only TypedArray.set: write truncation can succeed silently.

latentPortProtocolRisk.status: Confirmed in an isolated real MessageChannel fixture; not observed or established as a cause of the 96MP failure.

owner.mechanism: A null request throws while destructuring data. The catch dereferences data.id again, and tail.catch(()=>{}) swallows this second TypeError. No response or terminal endpoint failure is published.
owner.proof: A subsequent ordered read marker id999 returns [41,42,43,44], proving the owner queue advanced, while the original id1 read remains pending.

reader.mechanism: A null reply throws on data.id before resolving or rejecting any pending request.
reader.proof: The fixture captures TypeError at portable-byte-store.js:56:56 and receives a subsequent ordered marker, while the original read remains pending.

latentPortProtocolRisk.cleanup: Both pending reads reject CANCELLED only when the fixture explicitly disposes their reader. All ports are closed. A 1000ms fixture-only watchdog bounds cleanup/markers; success is based on ordered barriers rather than waiting for a timeout.
latentPortProtocolRisk.architecturalImplication: Worker envelope guards alone do not cover MessagePort RPC. A shared channel contract should validate both envelope directions, observe async handler failures, poison an unreadable endpoint once, and reject every pending call; unknown/null request ids cannot be replied to individually. Include messageerror, close/cancel, postMessage failure and peer shutdown. Do not classify opaque transport errors as allocator failures.
